title: Fix pytest BOM manifest gate on Python 3.11
intent: Restore the failing pytest BOM manifest gate by making BOM manifest paths platform-stable and regenerating the recorded AST hashes with the same Python 3.11 runtime used in GitHub Actions.

scope.out_of_scope_notes: No analyzer, schema, or workflow logic changes. The fix is limited to the BOM refresh utility and the generated BOM manifest artifact it owns.

what_changed: Normalized refresh_bom_manifest.py relative-path serialization to POSIX form with as_posix(), preventing Windows-only backslashes from being written into the shared manifest
Kept the refresh utility lint-clean while preserving behavior by modernizing a few local type hints and using importlib for the existing dynamic helper import
Regenerated tests/contracts/bom_manifest.json under Python 3.11 so the recorded script AST hashes match the GitHub Actions runtime and the manifest uses stable forward-slash paths
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: Refreshing the manifest alone would fix this checkout today but would allow a future Windows refresh to break Linux CI again. Normalizing the stored paths removes that portability trap while the regenerated Python 3.11 hashes address the current pytest failure.

commands_run: conda run -n py311 python -m ruff check scripts/refresh_bom_manifest.py
conda run -n py311 python -m pytest tests/test_bom_manifest_gate.py tests/test_bom_js_ts_surface.py tests/test_release_bom_contract.py::test_release_bom_is_buildable_and_self_consistent -q
test_results: BOM manifest refreshed successfully under Python 3.11
10 targeted BOM and release-contract pytest checks passed
verification.notes: I also inspected the failing GitHub Actions job logs for job 89640614655 before changing code. The original CI failure was an AST hash mismatch in tests/test_bom_manifest_gate.py for scripts/check_release_bom_consistency.py; local reproduction under Python 3.11 additionally exposed the manifest path separator portability problem that this patch closes.
